Sam (PM): Quick sync — sketched a few options for the eval-run header CTAs. Do we want primary action to be ‘Approve run’ or ‘Open scorecard’? Jake (Design): My take: primary should be the most common end state. For teams, that’s usually inspect -> approve, but not always. Maybe primary = ‘Open scorecard’ and secondary = ‘Approve run’? Maria (Product): Data question: what % of runs get approved straight from the list vs opened first? Alex (Eng): From logs last quarter ~38% opened scorecard, ~27% approved from list, rest rerun/assign. So open scorecard is more frequent. Ava (A11y): Accessibility-wise, primary action should be text-descriptive. ‘Open scorecard’ is clearer than generic ‘Approve’. Also need ARIA labels for the CTA so screen readers see context (e.g., `aria-label="Open scorecard for Eval Run 202"`). Jake (Design): Good point. Also thinking about affordance: a compact icon-only approve button next to each test might be tempting but loses discoverability. Maybe add a hover tooltip and keyboard shortcut hint `a` to approve focused item. Sam (PM): I like keyboard shortcut, but keep a clear fallback for mouse users. We also need to avoid accidental bulk approvals. Maria (Product): Proposal: Header primary = ‘Open scorecard’ (solid), secondary = ‘Approve run’ (outline, with confirmation). Per-row quick approve = small icon but requires two-step: click becomes inline confirm / or `Cmd+Enter` to confirm. Alex (Eng): Implementation note: inline confirm can be a transient popover. We should debounce accidental double-clicks. Also add `data-qa` attributes for E2E tests: `data-qa=approve-inline-btn` and `data-qa=approve-confirm`. Ava (A11y): For keyboard + screen reader: when inline confirm appears, move focus into it and use a live region: `
Approval pending. Press Enter to confirm.
`. Also ensure focus returns to the row after action completes. Jake (Design): Visuals: approval success state = green chip with check and label ‘Approved’, failure = red outline with error icon. Ensure contrast ratio 4.5:1 for the text in chips. Sam (PM): Copy nuance: confirmation modal copy should say why they’re approving — "Approving this run will mark X tests as passed and update the baseline. Proceed?" Add a link to the diff summary inside the modal. Maria (Product): Related microcopy: bulk-approve CTA should mention scope: ‘Approve all visible tests (filtered)’. Users forget the filter context. Alex (Eng): Backend note: approving a run triggers baseline update job. We should surface a small progress indicator in the header and disable approve until job ack. `deploy-bot` can post status updates. deploy-bot: baseline-update job queued for run 202. ETA ~30s. Ava (A11y): A11y nit: When the header progress indicator appears, expose it to SR via `role=status` and polite live region, not assertive. Non-interruptive. Jake (Design): One more UX question: show regression diff toggle (unified / split) in header or inside scorecard? I vote header — makes it discoverable for quick triage. Sam (PM): Agree header. Put a small label: `Diff view: Unified | Split` with persisted preference. Maria (Product): Finalize: I'll update the mocks with primary=Open scorecard, secondary=Approve run (with modal), inline icon approve with inline confirm, diff toggle in header, and accessibility hooks per Ava. I'll post updated Figma link in this thread. Jake (Design): Thanks — will do a quick accessibility contrast pass after the figma link. :eyes: Alex (Eng): Will stub the `data-qa` and ARIA hooks in the feature branch. Sam (PM): Awesome. Follow-ups: Maria to post Figma + copy, Alex to add QA hooks, Ava to review SR flow. Target PR by end of week. Maria (Product): Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/scorecard-cta-ux — comments enabled. Jake (Design): Left first pass comments on spacing and tooltip wording. Ava (A11y): I'll run a screen-reader walkthrough tomorrow and report any focus traps. Alex (Eng): Noted. I'll add a small e2e test for approve flows. Sam (PM): Thanks all. Closing the loop here — will sync in next standup.
